title: Desertification Forecasting in Semi-Arid Regions: Using Deep Learning to Probe the Observability Limits of Land Degradation Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2610.13406v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Forecasting desertification has received far less attention than mapping it. We use a convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) trained on ten annual Earth Observation (EO) variables (2000-2023) over the semi-arid state of Cear\'a, Brazil, on a 256x206 grid at roughly 2.2 km resolution, to measure how much of the year-to-year evolution of a MapBiomas-derived degradation index (IDV) can be predicted from satellite data. The network predicts a bounded change on top of the last observed state, is trained in two stages (single-step, then recursive rollout) and is evaluated on a contiguous spatial and temporal holdout. State-wide mean IDV rose from 0.238 to 0.350 between 2000 and 2023, about 0.005 per year, but cell-level change is dominated by year-to-year jumps, and a gradient-boosting model given all channels explains only 4.7% of its variance. translated_title: 半干旱地区的荒漠化预测：利用深度学习探究土地退化动态的可观测性极限
translated_abstract: 荒漠化的预测所受到的关注远少于荒漠化制图。我们使用一个卷积长短期记忆网络，在巴西半干旱的塞阿拉州上，基于2000至2023年的十种年度地球观测（EO）变量，以约2.2公里分辨率的256×206网格进行训练，以衡量卫星数据能在多大程度上预测MapBiomas衍生退化指数（IDV）的逐年演变。该网络在最后观测状态之上预测一个有界的变化量，采用两阶段训练（先单步预测，再递归展开），并在连续的空间与时间保留集上进行评估。2000年至2023年间，全州平均IDV从0.238上升至0.350，约每年0.005，但像元级别的变化以逐年跳变为主，一个输入全部通道的梯度提升模型仅能解释其方差的4.7%。相对于这一上限，ConvLSTM将提前一年预测的RMSE相对持续性基线降低了1.6%，提前四年降低了4.4%……
tldr: 该研究用ConvLSTM模型基于卫星观测数据预测巴西塞阿拉州土地退化指数的逐年演变，发现该指数的像元级变化以难以预测的逐年跳变为主（梯度提升模型仅能解释4.7%的方差），而ConvLSTM仍能相对持续性基线将提前一至四年预测的RMSE降低1.6%至4.4%，从而揭示了土地退化动态的可观测性极限。
en_tdlr: By training a ConvLSTM on ten annual Earth Observation variables (2000–2023) over Ceará, Brazil, this study shows that cell-level changes in a MapBiomas-derived degradation index are dominated by largely unpredictable year-to-year jumps (only 4.7% of variance explained by gradient boosting), yet the model still lowers RMSE by 1.6% (one year ahead) and 4.4% (four years ahead) relative to persistence, probing the observability limits of land degradation dynamics.
